result.topic_en: A continuation of Table A, dated 2 Feb 1798, listing digit sequences (apparently periods of continued-fraction-type expansions) for primes of the form 4n+1 between about 1861 and 2081; it adds a count of such primes between 2000 and 3000 and a formula giving a solution of P² − AQ² = ±1 from the expansion.

methods.what: Construction of a solution of the Pell-type equation P² − AQ² = ±1 from the product of the terms (k+√A) and the product of the denominators d of the expansion of √A
methods.quote:
$(k+\sqrt{A})(k'+\sqrt{A})\ldots(k+\sqrt{A}) = K$
$d.d'.d''\ldots\quad d = D$
$P = [-\ldots-]\ \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{K}{D} \pm \frac{D}{k}\right)$
$Q = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{K}{D\sqrt{A}} \mp \frac{k}{D\sqrt{A}}\right)$
